title: the Glass Steppe Rising
premise: Beatrix Montrose, a cartographer who maps realms that shouldn't exist, keeps the ledgers of the Glass Steppe Guild, which trades in impossible things. When she discovers tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies — and finds the name of a stranger, Elias Vane, written beside it — she pulls him into the guild's world just as its assassins arrive to claim him. Elias carries a secret buried in his blood: he is the last vessel of the Steppe's sealed god, and if the prophecy completes, an ancient war reignites. Hunted by the guild's mistress, the zealots of the Ash Choir, and his own awakening power, Beatrix must choose between preserving her carefully mapped world and breaking every law that holds it together. In the end, she rewrites the ledger itself — trading her own name out of existence to unmake the prophecy, leaving Elias alive but unmapped, and the Steppe free at a price no one will ever remember she paid.
about_author: Hazel Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that turned out not to exist. She writes fantasy about people who keep records of dangerous truths.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Beatrix closes the guild's accounts on a night like any other, cataloguing traded impossibilities: bottled thunder, a debt paid in years. She notices a new entry in her own handwriting she never wrote. POV: Beatrix. Beat: quiet unease beneath routine competence.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Cross-checking anomalies, Beatrix opens the sealed Century Codex and finds tonight's date — and beside it, a stranger's name: Elias Vane. The ink is still wet after a hundred years. POV: Beatrix. Beat: dread crystallizing into obsession.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Beatrix tracks Elias, a night-shift surveyor with no records before three years ago. When she confronts him, the Codex in her bag grows warm and his shadow moves wrong. POV: Elias. Beat: disorientation turning to fear as his ordinary life cracks open.

chapters.title: Assassins Keep Business Hours
chapters.summary: Guild enforcers arrive to collect Elias per an old contract Beatrix never signed. She burns the writ, declares him guild property, and drags him into the Steppe through a door drawn in chalk. POV: Beatrix. Beat: reckless commitment; point of no return.

chapters.title: The Glass Steppe
chapters.summary: Elias sees the guild's true territory: a plain of fused glass where geography obeys ledgers instead of laws. Beatrix explains the trade in impossible things — and that someone has been buying pieces of him for years. POV: Elias. Beat: awe curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Mistress of Accounts
chapters.summary: Guildmistress Sarelle Voss receives them, courteous and terrifying, and reveals the contract: Elias was sold at birth by his own mother. She wants delivery by month's end or Beatrix forfeits everything. POV: Beatrix. Beat: the cost of protection made explicit.

chapters.title: What Sleeps Under the Salt
chapters.summary: An old cartographer, Ivo Quill, shows them the first map ever drawn of the Steppe — and the god-shaped absence at its center. Elias touches it and the glass sings. POV: Elias. Beat: revelation; he is the vessel of the sealed god.

chapters.title: The Ash Choir Sings
chapters.summary: Zealots who worship the sealed god attack the archive, seeking to complete the prophecy by force. Ivo dies holding the door. Beatrix and Elias escape with half a map. POV: Beatrix. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Ledger Law
chapters.summary: Hiding in a border town, Beatrix teaches Elias how the Steppe works: debts are binding, names are currency, and the law is whatever is written first. He learns to write himself small. POV: Elias. Beat: fragile partnership deepening into trust.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: To buy passage, Beatrix trades a memory of her sister. Elias watches her pay without flinching and understands what survival costs here — and what it will cost her to save him. POV: Elias. Beat: tenderness shadowed by guilt.

chapters.title: Voss Opens the Books
chapters.summary: Sarelle audits Beatrix's entire career, finding every mercy she ever extended, and offers a deal: deliver Elias, and all debts forgiven. Beatrix asks for one night to decide. POV: Beatrix. Beat: temptation; the corruption of institutional power laid bare.

chapters.title: Prophecy Is Just a Draft
chapters.summary: Elias realizes the Codex isn't predicting — it's drafting, and drafts can be edited. But editing requires a hand the god will trust: his own blood as ink. POV: Elias. Beat: hope with a terrible price attached.

chapters.title: The Choir's Cathedral of Salt
chapters.summary: Captured by the Ash Choir, Elias is shown their vision: the god risen, the war refought, the world remade in glory. Their leader is gentle, sincere, and utterly certain. POV: Elias. Beat: horror at righteous conviction.

chapters.title: Beatrix Breaks In
chapters.summary: Beatrix spends nearly everything — names, memories, years — to forge herself into the cathedral's ledger as 'staff.' She walks past guards who cannot see what is not written. POV: Beatrix. Beat: sacrifice escalating; love expressed as accounting.

chapters.title: The God Wakes
chapters.summary: The Choir begins the rite early. Elias feels the god rising through him like floodwater, offering peace in exchange for surrender. Beatrix reaches him at the last line of the liturgy. POV: Elias. Beat: climax begins; identity versus annihilation.

chapters.title: Amendments
chapters.summary: Together they fight the rite with revision: Beatrix strikes lines from the prophecy aloud while Elias bleeds corrections onto the page. The Choir's certainty shatters as their text betrays them. POV: Beatrix. Beat: climax; words as weapons.

chapters.title: Sarelle Collects
chapters.summary: Voss arrives with the guild's full weight, intending to seize the god regardless of which side wins. Beatrix invokes an ancient clause: the ledger's keeper may settle any account with herself. POV: Beatrix. Beat: the final price named.

chapters.title: Written Out
chapters.summary: Beatrix trades her name, her history, her place in every record, to void the contract and seal the god asleep forever. Elias holds her as the ink takes her, screaming that there must be another way. POV: Elias. Beat: devastating climax resolution.

chapters.title: The Unmapped Woman
chapters.summary: The Steppe stabilizes; the Choir scatters; Voss, bound by the settled account, withdraws. Elias searches the glass for any trace of Beatrix and finds only a compass rose drawn in chalk, pointing nowhere. POV: Elias. Beat: hollow victory.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Forgot
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Elias runs the guild's accounts badly but honestly, honoring her methods. He discovers entries in an unknown hand — hers, surviving outside every ledger because she was never written in them. POV: Elias. Beat: grief pierced by impossible hope.

chapters.title: A Door Drawn in Chalk
chapters.summary: Following the orphaned entries, Elias finds a realm off every map where a woman with no name has begun drawing new coastlines. She doesn't remember him. He introduces himself anyway. POV: Elias. Beat: bittersweet beginning.

chapters.title: The Glass Steppe Rising
chapters.summary: Epilogue: the Steppe itself, freed from prophecy, begins to grow wild beyond its ledgers for the first time in a thousand years. Somewhere in the new growth, two sets of footprints head toward unmapped country. POV: omniscient. Beat: renewal; the world outgrowing its keepers.
